items.h: Trump to meet Xi and Putin in Shenzhen next week; White House says nuclear arms cuts on the agenda
items.t: The White House said President Donald Trump will hold a three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of next week’s APEC summit in Shenzhen, and assistant White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales said he “will discuss reducing nuclear weapons” (Anadolu Agency, reported November 14). A senior U.S. official said Washington does not expect an agreement, calling the meeting “the entry point, the first conversation” at the leader level.

items.h: IRGC claims it hit a U.S. radar in Bahrain; CENTCOM says it downed two drones, with no damage
items.t: Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it targeted a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain on November 13 in retaliation for a November 12 attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik (Drop Site News). U.S. Central Command denied the claim, saying U.S. forces shot down two one-way attack drones launched toward Bahrain and that there were no injuries or damage (Fox News).

items.h: Iran tells IAEA it won’t resume monitoring talks, citing “threats” from the U.S. president
items.t: Iran told the International Atomic Energy Agency in a letter that monitoring talks cannot proceed amid “a series of persistent, explicit, and public threats by the President of the United States of America,” according to a confidential IAEA report sent to member states on November 13 and cited by The Associated Press. The report voiced growing concern about the Isfahan fuel enrichment plant, saying the agency does not know its exact location or whether it holds nuclear material.

items.h: Turkey and Qatar sign mutual defense pact
items.t: Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan and Qatar’s emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, signed five agreements, including a mutual defense pact, on November 13 at the 12th Turkey-Qatar High Strategic Committee meeting at the Dolmabahçe presidential office in Istanbul (Anadolu Agency, Khaleej Times). Erdoğan said Turkey will keep working with Doha to prevent a return to war (Khaleej Times).

items.h: Putin meets U.S. envoys; Kremlin says what could be a record prisoner swap is in the works
items.t: After Russian President Vladimir Putin met U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner at the Kremlin on November 12, presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said the talks would continue and that the terms of what would likely be the largest prisoner exchange to date are being finalized. Witkoff said, “We’ve set a new meeting.”

items.h: Zelensky says Starshield speed cap is back; SpaceX official says “this is false”
items.t: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on November 12 that the Starshield satellite terminals used by Ukraine’s military are being systematically capped at 161 km/h (100 mph), making Russian jet-powered drones far harder to intercept. A SpaceX official told the U.S. outlet TWZ, “This is false,” and “There has been no change.”

items.h: Trump says the U.S. doesn’t need an Iran deal; on force, “it’s possible I would do it right now”
items.t: President Donald Trump posted on social media on November 12 (U.S. time): “We don’t need a deal with Iran. Those days have long since passed.” The same day, asked by a Salem News Channel host what he would do if Iran threatened U.S. allies and ships, he said that if he saw things going the other way he would act, and “it’s possible I would do it right now.”

items.h: CENTCOM dismisses report it advised Israel to prepare for renewed Iran operations
items.t: Israeli public broadcaster KAN, citing a U.S. official, reported that U.S. Central Command advised Israel to prepare for a possible resumption of military operations against Iran in the near future. In comments to Anadolu Agency published November 13, a CENTCOM official dismissed the account as “pure speculation” and said there had been no change to the U.S. force posture in the region.

items.h: Kremlin points to first-ever three-way summit China is planning in Shenzhen
items.t: Presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said on November 12 that a meeting between Russian President Vladimir Putin and President Donald Trump is planned on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, and that he hopes the trilateral summit China is organizing there, the first of its kind, will help stabilize the international situation. The Kremlin did not name the three parties; Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on November 10 that a U.S.-China-Russia leaders’ meeting on the APEC sidelines “should be possible” (Reuters).

items.h: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang resigns as CEO; CFO Colette Kress named interim chief
items.t: Nvidia announced on November 12 (U.S. time) that Jensen Huang had resigned as president, CEO and board member, effective immediately, and that CFO Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while keeping her current role. The company gave no reason, and the board has begun a search for a permanent CEO.

items.h: U.S.-brokered Abu Dhabi talks yield a deal in principle on a prisoner swap, no breakthrough
items.t: Two days of U.S.-brokered talks in Abu Dhabi ended November 11 with Ukraine's chief negotiator, foreign intelligence chief Rustem Umerov, and Russian presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky saying the sides had agreed in principle on a large-scale prisoner exchange. There was no major progress toward ending the war, and U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner (President Donald Trump's son-in-law) are set to meet President Vladimir Putin in Moscow on November 12.

items.h: Ghalibaf says Iran and Oman set the rules in Hormuz; Vance reported to weigh meeting Rezaei
items.t: Iranian parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf told Al Jazeera in an interview published November 11 that the Strait of Hormuz is “governed by the laws of the two littoral states that border it,” Iran and Oman, and repeated that the U.S. must lift its blockade and sanctions, among other conditions, before talks can begin. The same day, The Wall Street Journal reported that Vice President JD Vance was considering a face-to-face meeting with Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, and that the discussions were preliminary.

items.h: Trump says he wants “a total victory, not a 93 percent victory” in Iran, says ending the war is “just a question of when”
items.t: Speaking at Arlington National Cemetery on Veterans Day, November 11, President Donald Trump said of the Iran war, “We won,” and that it was “just a question of when we want to end it.” He added: “We want to make sure we have a total victory, not a 93 percent victory.”

items.h: Eisenkot urges Netanyahu in a letter to hold off on “dangerous moves” until a new government is in place
items.t: Gadi Eisenkot, who has been tasked with forming Israel's next government, wrote to caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on November 11 urging him to refrain from dangerous moves that can wait until a new government is sworn in. Gulf News, citing Israeli media, reported that Netanyahu had pushed for action against Iran despite objections from IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir, a claim that has not been confirmed.

items.h: Taiwan's defense minister says China ran “area denial drills” in the western Pacific with the Liaoning carrier group
items.t: Taiwanese Defense Minister Wellington Koo told reporters at the Legislative Yuan in Taipei on November 10 that China “has indeed conducted area denial drills in the Western Pacific” with the Liaoning carrier group and other formations, Reuters reported. National Security Council Secretary-General Joseph Wu had said that as of November 3 more than 100 Chinese navy and coast guard vessels were deployed across the western Pacific. China has not formally announced the drills.

items.h: Indonesian Vice President Gibran hands his resignation to the MPR a day after House factions moved to impeach him
items.t: Indonesian Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka delivered his resignation to leaders of the People's Consultative Assembly (MPR) at the parliament complex in Jakarta on the morning of November 12, local time, Antara reported. A day earlier, every faction in the House of Representatives had submitted a motion invoking the House's right to express an opinion, the first step toward impeachment.

items.h: Rubio says strikes on Iran are unnecessary if economic pressure achieves the same goal; Iran's Rezaei denies talks
items.t: Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking in Paris on November 10 after a G7 foreign ministers' meeting, said there was no need to strike Iran: “We don't need to conduct military strikes if we're achieving the same objective through economic means and economic pressure.” The same day, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, called reports of talks with Washington “complete lies” in a broadcast interview and said the Strait of Hormuz would stay closed until all seven of Iran's conditions were met, according to Anadolu.

items.h: U.S.-brokered Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi run about four hours on day one; Rubio says they appear to have been “very productive”
items.t: Russian and Ukrainian delegations met for about four hours in Abu Dhabi on November 10 in talks mediated by the United States, with a second day set for November 11, the AP reported. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky called the session constructive and quite substantive and said it covered prisoner exchanges, the return of detained civilians and of children deported from Ukraine, and security guarantees.

items.h: Tanker struck northeast of Lima, Oman; ship attacks around Hormuz hit a wartime monthly high of 37 in October
items.t: The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations center (UKMTO) said a tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile in waters northeast of Lima, Oman, on November 10 but did not say who was responsible. Reuters reported that, according to the Washington Institute for Near East Policy, 37 ships were attacked in and around the Strait of Hormuz in October, the most in any month since the war began, and that 10 more attacks had been recorded so far in November.

items.h: Indonesian Vice President Gibran offers his resignation to Prabowo
items.t: State Secretary Prasetyo Hadi said on November 10 that Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka had offered his resignation during a meeting of more than two hours with President Prabowo Subianto. It was not disclosed whether Prabowo had accepted it. Gibran has been under pressure since a court found that his educational documents did not meet the eligibility requirements to run in the election.

items.h: Trump says "Iran militarily is effectively over" after meeting Qatar's prime minister, but keeps blockade
items.t: President Donald Trump, after meeting Qatari Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani at the White House on November 9, said there was momentum toward ending the war but that the naval blockade would remain in place. On Truth Social, he said renewed strikes were quite unlikely. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, called it fake news about imaginary talks.

items.h: China extends rare earth export control pause to January 10, 2027, and delays other countermeasures
items.t: China's Commerce Ministry said in a short statement on November 9 that it would extend by two months, to January 10, 2027, its suspension of the export controls on rare earths and other materials that it expanded in October 2025. Reuters reported that the move was part of a wider extension, announced the same day, of China's suspension of trade countermeasures and tariffs.

items.h: U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks resume in Abu Dhabi, the first since February in Geneva
items.t: U.S.-brokered three-way talks with Russia and Ukraine were set to resume in Abu Dhabi on November 10, TASS reported. TASS said presidential aide Vladimir Medinsky leads the Russian delegation and that the three sides last met in Geneva on February 18.

items.h: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards for supermarket cyberattack, summons envoy
items.t: Paris prosecutors said on November 9 that Iran's Revolutionary Guards were behind the October 12 cyberattack that remotely tampered with refrigeration systems in French supermarkets, and sought international arrest warrants for the leaders of the affiliated Shahid Kaveh group. Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Iran's ambassador was being summoned and that sanctions would be imposed at the European level.

items.h: GOP Rep. Massie files impeachment articles against Hegseth over the Iran war
items.t: Rep. Thomas Massie, a Kentucky Republican, on November 9 filed eight articles of impeachment accusing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth of, among other things, abusing his powers and illegally waging war on Iran. Euronews reported that a vote could come as early as November 11. Trump said on November 9 that he backed Hegseth.

items.h: Herzog taps Eisenkot to form Israel's next government; 46 lawmakers backed Netanyahu
items.t: Israeli President Isaac Herzog formally tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming a new government on November 8 at the President's Residence in Jerusalem. Sixty-seven lawmakers recommended Eisenkot and 46 recommended Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Eisenkot has 28 days, which can be extended by 14.

items.h: Rubio calls Iran's demands "outrageous"; Araghchi says "it is the White House's turn to choose"
items.t: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on November 8 pointed to Iran's two-day plan, under which the U.S. would carry out agreed measures on the first day and Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz on the second. "American voters have made their choice. Now it is the White House's turn to choose," he said. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the same day that he would not say the two sides were on the verge of a breakthrough, calling Iran's demands outrageous and unrealistic.

items.h: CENTCOM launches "Iron Gate" task force to block Iran's land and Caspian trade
items.t: U.S. Central Command said on November 7 it had launched Task Force Iron Gate to cut off advanced weapons, dual-use technology, sanctioned materials and illicit revenue moving across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea. CENTCOM also said U.S. aircraft struck and stopped the cargo ship Huda in the Gulf of Oman the same day after it ignored warnings.

items.h: Trump says Ukraine will likely "end up with a little bit different shape" ahead of Abu Dhabi talks
items.t: In a CBS "60 Minutes" interview that aired on November 8, President Donald Trump said Ukraine would likely "end up with a little bit different shape" after the war and that a deal was very close. The Kremlin had earlier said three-way talks among the U.S., Russia and Ukraine would be held in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11.

items.h: Russia strikes Ukraine's grid, Black Sea ports; more than 600,000 lose power in Dnipropetrovsk
items.t: Ukraine's air force said Russia launched 164 drones and three missiles between 6 p.m. on November 7 and 8 a.m. on November 8 local time, and that 137 drones were shot down or neutralized. DTEK said more than 600,000 residents in the Dnipropetrovsk region lost power, and Russia's Defense Ministry claimed it hit three cargo ships around Odesa, a claim that could not be verified.

items.h: Japan seeks equal treatment for Takaichi at APEC; formal summit with China unlikely, Bloomberg says
items.t: Bloomberg reported on November 9, citing people familiar with the matter, that Japan has asked China to confirm Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi will be treated like other leaders at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen on November 18–19. A formal Japan-China summit is unlikely, with no more than a handshake expected, the report said.

items.h: China's factory-gate prices rise 5.7 percent in October; consumer prices up 0.7 percent
items.t: China's National Bureau of Statistics said on November 9 that the producer price index rose 5.7 percent in October from a year earlier and the consumer price index rose 0.7 percent. Investing.com said the producer price increase was the fastest since June 2022.

items.h: Trump says U.S. knocked out Iranian anti-aircraft device "in about 15 minutes, maybe five" in first strike since midterms
items.t: President Donald Trump said on November 6 local time that U.S. forces had hit an anti-aircraft device Iran built, calling the strike "minor." Iranian state media reported the sound of two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island. The AP said it was the first U.S. strike since the midterms; the extent of the damage was unclear.

items.h: Qatar proposes two-day bridge deal; Iran reviewing it, Mideast officials say
items.t: Two Middle East officials told the AP on November 6 that Qatar has proposed a plan under which, on day one, the U.S. would lift its naval blockade and return some of Iran's frozen funds and Iran would allow IAEA inspections of bombed facilities, and on day two Iran would reopen the Strait of Hormuz. They said Iran is reviewing the plan. The White House declined to comment.

items.h: Russia hits Kyiv with ballistic missiles; Northern Bridge damaged, five injured
items.t: Ukraine's air force said Russia attacked across Ukraine with missiles, including ballistic missiles, and 172 Shahed-type drones starting at 6 p.m. local time on November 6. As of 9 a.m. on November 7, it had shot down or neutralized four missiles and 149 drones, and the attack was continuing. Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said the Northern Bridge was damaged and closed to traffic in both directions, and that five people, including a 14-year-old girl, were injured.

items.h: New Zealand early count puts National-led governing coalition on track for majority
items.t: With 10 percent of the vote counted in New Zealand's November 7 election, National had 31.2 percent, Labour 28.3 percent, ACT 11.3 percent and NZ First 9.7 percent, with the Greens at 12.7 percent, putting the governing coalition on track for a majority, AAP reported. Official results are due by November 27.

items.h: Iran's Rezaei: no Hormuz reopening, no talks until U.S. meets seven conditions
items.t: Iran has sent the U.S. a nuclear proposal through Qatar but will discuss it only after Washington meets seven demands, including lifting sanctions, returning frozen assets and paying war reparations, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on November 5. Mohsen Rezaei, Iran's top security official, made the same point while visiting Russia.

items.h: Nasdaq plunges 5.5 percent into correction on fears of Democratic AI curbs
items.t: The Nasdaq Composite fell 5.52 percent to close at 24,315.00 on November 5, entering correction territory, while the S&P 500 lost 4.36 percent, the Seoul Economic Daily reported. The selloff was blamed on fears that Democrats, after winning control of Congress, will tighten rules on AI and data centers.

items.h: Iran claims a string of tankers hit mines near Hormuz
items.t: Iran's military and the Revolutionary Guards said on November 5 that tankers and a tugboat caught fire after mine strikes and other incidents in waters south and east of the Strait of Hormuz. Taken together, the Iranian statements claim at least five tankers and one tug; none of the claims has been independently verified. January Brent futures settled up 3.88 percent at $98.29 a barrel that day, according to the Seoul Economic Daily.

items.h: Melania Trump hosts Russian, Ukrainian officials: "something more enduring than a temporary ceasefire"
items.t: Melania Trump met Kirill Dmitriev, President Vladimir Putin's special envoy, and Dmytro Lubinets, Ukraine's parliamentary human rights commissioner, among others, at the White House on November 5 to mark a six-day truce in Oleshky, in the Kherson region, that ended November 1, and the evacuation of nearly 800 residents. President Donald Trump told reporters it would be "a big agreement" that "might involve all of Europe."

items.h: Somalia's top court rules term extension unlawful; president announces chief justice's dismissal
items.t: Somalia's Supreme Court ruled on November 5 that President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's term extension was unlawful and ordered a new agreement among political parties within 30 days and elections within 90, AFP reported. Before the ruling was published, the presidency announced it was dismissing Chief Justice Bashe Yusuf Ahmed.

items.h: Oil plunges more than 8 percent after U.S. midterms; Brent at $94
items.t: Brent fell 8.6 percent to $94.66 a barrel as of 1:06 p.m. ET on November 4, with WTI at $88.08, according to OilPrice.com. With Democrats now controlling both chambers of Congress, markets are trying to gauge where the U.S.-Iran war is headed, The National reported.

items.h: Vance blames Iran war for GOP midterm losses
items.t: Vice President JD Vance wrote on X that the Iran war cost Republicans in the midterms and that "any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there," OilPrice.com reported on November 4.

items.h: Zelensky tells Witkoff, Kushner postwar guarantees must be ironclad
items.t: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said he spoke for about 90 minutes on November 4 with U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner about Patriot interceptors and postwar security guarantees. In Brussels the same day, the U.S., Ukraine, NATO, Germany, France and the U.K. coordinated positions ahead of trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11.

items.h: Indonesia's military mobilizes thousands in capital after presidential wiretap case
items.t: Indonesia's military said it was mobilizing thousands of troops to tighten security in the capital after President Prabowo Subianto on November 4 fired his chief of staff, Listyo Sigit Prabowo, who had been arrested on suspicion of illegally wiretapping the president and others, Reuters reported. A presidential spokesman said the conduct could border on treason.

items.h: South Korea's Defense Ministry seeks to widen Cheonghae Unit zone south of Oman
items.t: A revised Defense Ministry motion extending the Cheonghae Unit's deployment cleared a vice-ministerial meeting on November 5, SBS reported. It widens the unit's zone from the Gulf of Aden to south of Oman's port of Duqm and adds a P-8 maritime patrol aircraft, an explosive ordnance disposal team and unmanned mine-countermeasure systems. A ministry official said direct detection of the Strait of Hormuz or Iranian territory would be limited, Financial News reported.

items.h: Democrats retake Senate, projected to win House in U.S. midterms
items.t: Democrats flipped Republican-held Senate seats in North Carolina, Ohio, Texas, Kansas, Iowa and South Carolina in the November 3 midterms, winning control of the chamber, the AP reported. NBC, CNN and others projected that Democrats would also win a House majority, but the AP had not called the House as of late November 3.

items.h: Russia pounds Ukraine's grid; Kyiv says drones targeted nuclear-plant substation
items.t: Ukrainian Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said Russia hit power plants and substations with 289 drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles starting early on November 3, sending three drones toward a substation critical to the stable operation of the Khmelnytskyi nuclear power plant, and that Ukraine had notified the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA). Grid operator Ukrenergo imposed emergency blackouts in Kyiv and several other regions.

items.h: Trump confirms strike on Iranian air-defense site, calls it a "minor attack"
items.t: President Donald Trump said in a Fox News interview on November 3 that Iran had built an anti-aircraft facility and that "as soon as it was completed, we hit it last night," calling it a "minor attack." A U.S. official told the AP on November 2 that U.S. forces had struck Iranians who used surface-to-air missiles against them in the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian state media reported explosions on Qeshm Island and elsewhere, and Iranian Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi said Iran had a legitimate right to self-defense.

items.h: Trump says he and Netanyahu agreed to end U.S. aid to Israel by year's end
items.t: Trump said in a Fox News interview on November 3 that the U.S. gives Israel $4 billion a year but that he and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "made a deal months ago that we're stopping," adding that "by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel." The current memorandum of understanding provides about $3.8 billion a year over 10 years starting in 2019; Netanyahu has previously spoken of phasing out aid over a decade, and his office did not immediately comment.

items.h: Russian bombs hit aid-distribution school in Zaporizhzhia region; Ukraine says 26 killed
items.t: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on November 2 that a school distributing humanitarian aid in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, and a shelter inside it were hit one after another by Russian aerial bombs, killing 26 people, and that nine more bombs fell after the first strike. Regional governor Mykhailo Semikin said 27 people were missing.

items.h: U.S. plans three-way talks with Russia, Ukraine in Abu Dhabi November 10–11, senior official says
items.t: A senior U.S. official told Reuters on November 2 that the U.S. will hold three-way talks with Ukrainian and Russian delegations in Abu Dhabi on November 10–11 on postwar security arrangements, de-escalation, humanitarian measures and ending the war. Special envoy Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are expected to represent the U.S., the official said.

items.h: Iranian negotiators leave Doha as draft deal circulates; Iran ties final deal to blockade's end
items.t: Iranian negotiators left Doha, where they had been meeting Qatari mediators, on November 1, but not because the talks had stalled, an official briefed on the negotiations told Reuters on November 2. A draft deal with the U.S. is circulating and a follow-up meeting is possible, the official said. Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said there will be no final deal and no reopening of the strait until the U.S. naval blockade ends and Iran's demands are met.

items.h: U.S. warns Gulf allies of possible Iran strikes as soon as November 4, report says
items.t: MS NOW, citing three senior Gulf Arab officials, reported that Washington warned Gulf allies that a brief but intense round of strikes on Iran could come as early as November 4, the day after the midterm elections; the White House said it does not comment on military plans. President Trump told reporters at Mar-a-Lago in Florida on October 31 that one or two of Iran's remaining nuclear-related sites still had to be dealt with, "but we can do that in 10 minutes."

items.h: Araghchi says new proposal cuts Hormuz reopening to two days as Doha talks hit day three
items.t: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told Al Jazeera on October 31 that Iran had drawn up a proposal with Qatari mediators that would shorten the timeline for reopening the Strait of Hormuz to two days. Iran's negotiators held a third straight day of talks with Qatari mediators in Doha on November 1, and Araghchi said no final conclusion had yet been reached.

items.h: Mojtaba Khamenei orders forces to answer any threat immediately, without geographic limits
items.t: Iran's supreme leader, Mojtaba Khamenei, ordered the armed forces in an October 31 statement to meet any threat with an immediate, effective response unrestricted by geography, AFP reported. Army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia warned on state TV on November 1 that a new war could last longer than the last one.

items.h: Tanker struck off Saudi coast; Revolutionary Guards claim two tankers hit mines in Hormuz
items.t: The UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) said a tanker was hit by two unidentified projectiles 72 nautical miles east of Ras al-Khafji, Saudi Arabia, early on November 2 local time, and that all crew were accounted for. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed on November 1 that two tankers exploded after hitting mines while crossing the Strait of Hormuz on an unauthorized route; the claim has not been verified.
items.pl: Persian Gulf, east of Ras al-Khafji (Saudi Arabia)

items.h: Russia hits Ukraine's energy facilities with 433 drones, leaving hundreds of thousands without power
items.t: Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 433 drones starting at 6 p.m. local time on October 31 and that 371 had been shot down or neutralized as of 7:30 a.m. on November 1; President Zelensky said hundreds of thousands of households were without power. Russia's Defense Ministry said it shot down 47 Ukrainian drones between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. Moscow time on November 1.

items.h: Rubio: "I don't know if negotiated peace is achievable in Ukraine"
items.t: Secretary of State Marco Rubio told a press conference at the G20 foreign ministers' meeting in Atlanta on October 31, "I don't know if negotiated peace is achievable in Ukraine, that's what we're trying to find out." The three-way U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi are expected in early November, but no date has been set, the Kyiv Independent reported.

items.h: Unidentified object enters Latvian airspace near Russia, Belarus; residents told to stay indoors
items.t: Latvia's military said on November 1 that an unidentified flying object had entered airspace around Kraslava and Ludza in the country's southeast, warning residents to stay indoors, and that the all-clear came within an hour. It said it launched an interceptor drone but had it self-destruct to avoid crossing into Russian or Belarusian airspace; the object's origin has not been determined.

items.h: France's cost-of-living protests hit third weekend: 320,000 march, 290 arrested
items.t: Protests over the cost of living and conditions in schools drew 320,000 people across France on October 31, including 70,000 in Paris, according to authorities, marking a third straight weekend of demonstrations. The Interior Ministry reported at least 290 arrests, Al Jazeera reported; organizers claimed nearly 500,000, and police fired tear gas in Paris and Lyon.

items.h: Oman rescues 25 from burning tanker; Revolutionary Guards claim three tankers halted
items.t: Oman's Maritime Security Centre said on October 30 that its navy rescued 25 crew members from the RITI, a Panama-flagged tanker that caught fire after being attacked in the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guards claimed the same day that three tankers using unauthorized routes were halted after incidents including mine strikes; the U.S. military has denied the mine claims, and it is unclear whether the RITI is one of the three.

items.h: Kremlin opposes truce that gives Ukraine a respite; talks date in works with U.S.
items.t: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on October 30 that Russia opposes a ceasefire that would give Ukraine a respite and has no plans to halt fighting before the three-way talks in Abu Dhabi, TASS reported. Presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said the same day that the talks will be held in November and that coordination on a date with Washington has begun, though no specific date has been set.

items.h: Qatari mediators return to Tehran; Trump says Iran war will be "wrapped up soon"
items.t: Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on October 30 to push for a U.S.-Iran deal in coordination with Washington, an official briefed on the talks told Reuters, while a senior Iranian official called the proposals unacceptable. President Trump told Kansas City radio station KCMO the same day that the war is "going to get wrapped up soon," adding, "We need a guarantee there'll never be a nuclear weapon."

items.h: Standoff in Poland over bid to suspend top court chief; president turns his plane around
items.t: On October 30, Judge Anna Korwin-Piotrowska, one of the judges President Karol Nawrocki has refused to swear in, ordered the suspension of Constitutional Tribunal head Bogdan Święczkowski and his deputy, Bartłomiej Sochański. The tribunal's leadership rejected the order and called it a "coup d'état." Prime Minister Donald Tusk wrote, "Restoring the rule of law is our duty." Nawrocki, en route to Senegal for a state visit, turned his plane around to return to Poland.

items.h: Canada, EU launch Alliance for the Future; Canada aims to be first EU associate member
items.t: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, European Council President António Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen launched the Alliance for the Future at a summit in Montreal on October 30, with Canada working toward becoming the EU's first associate member, the prime minister's office said. The substance and scope of that status will be worked out over the coming months; the two sides also concluded negotiations on digital trade and competition agreements.

items.h: G20 foreign ministers' meeting opens in Atlanta with Lavrov; group photo scrapped
items.t: A two-day G20 foreign ministers' meeting hosted by Secretary of State Marco Rubio opened in Atlanta on October 30, with Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov attending and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi sending a representative, AFP reported. A planned group photo was canceled after some European officials balked at appearing alongside Lavrov.

items.h: State Department approves $2.1 billion sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine
items.t: The State Department said on October 30 it approved the possible sale to Ukraine of 500 Patriot PAC-3 missiles, plus parts and support, for an estimated $2.1 billion. Two people briefed on the decision said the missiles have not yet been built and are not expected to be delivered until the early 2030s, Al Jazeera and Reuters reported.

items.h: Tankers hit in Strait of Hormuz; Revolutionary Guards claim three struck mines
items.t: Britain's UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said a tanker leaving the strait was hit by an unknown projectile near Khasab, Oman, at around 8 p.m. local time on October 29. Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy claimed that over the previous 24 hours three tankers using an unauthorized southern route exploded and caught fire after hitting mines; the claim has not been independently verified.

items.h: Russian drone hits Dnipro train platform, killing 14
items.t: A Russian drone struck a platform at Dnipro station, where a Zaporizhzhia-bound train was waiting, during the day on October 29 local time, killing 14 people and wounding 14, said Oleksandr Hanzha, head of the Dnipropetrovsk regional military administration. Five more people were killed the same day in Chernihiv and Kremenchuk.

items.h: Iran's Tasnim says Tehran received Vance letter but has not replied
items.t: Iran's Tasnim news agency reported on October 29 that Tehran had received a letter from U.S. Vice President JD Vance to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, but had not yet responded, and that its seven conditions still stand. President Trump said the letter was about medical supplies and that he had not ordered talks to resume.

items.h: Israel finishes count: Netanyahu bloc at 53 seats, Likud largest party with 27
items.t: Likud won 27 seats and Yashar 21 with all votes counted, according to Central Elections Committee results released early on October 30 local time, the Times of Israel reported. By bloc, Netanyahu's has 53 seats, Eisenkot's 48 and Arab parties 19. Official results are slated to go to President Isaac Herzog on November 4.

items.h: Zelensky eyes Abu Dhabi talks with U.S., Russia November 6–10; Kremlin says Europe excluded
items.t: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said at a press conference with Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten in The Hague on October 28 that he hopes three-way talks with the U.S. and Russia will take place in Abu Dhabi between November 6 and 10, and that Kyiv is waiting for Washington's answer. Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov told Interfax that European countries will not be included in the talks, Al Jazeera reported the same day.

items.h: Iran, mediators discuss speeding up war-ending seven-day plan; official calls Qatari draft "unacceptable ideas"
items.t: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on X on October 28 that Tehran is "in close and ongoing contact with intermediaries" on ways to carry out the seven-day plan "in even less than a week." Reuters reported the same day that Qatari mediators handed Iran a new seven-day draft deal to end the war on October 25, and that a senior Iranian official involved in the talks called it "unacceptable ideas and not an offer."

items.h: North Korea fires about 10 short-range ballistic missiles into the East Sea from the Wonsan area
items.t: South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff said it detected about 10 short-range ballistic missiles North Korea fired from the Wonsan area into the East Sea at around 12:30 p.m. on October 29. The launch came six days after the Ministry of National Defense on October 23 proposed military talks on confirming the location of the Military Demarcation Line and restoring military communication lines, among other items; Pyongyang has not responded.

items.h: Israel count at 90 percent: Netanyahu bloc 53 seats, Eisenkot's 48, neither with a majority
items.t: With 89.8 percent of votes counted just after 9 p.m. local time on October 28, Central Elections Committee results put Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc at 53 seats, former military chief Gadi Eisenkot's bloc at 48 and Arab-led parties at a record 19, The Times of Israel reported. Roughly 430,000 to 480,000 double-envelope ballots remain, and official results will be published November 4.

items.h: Putin tells 48 African nations Russian business does not engage in "neo-colonial exploitation"
items.t: The third Russia-Africa summit was held in Moscow on October 28 with 48 African countries represented, 22 of them by their leaders, Al Jazeera reported. President Vladimir Putin said, "Our business does not engage in the predatory, neo-colonial exploitation of natural and human resources," and Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed said on X the same day that his country had received 12 Russian Su-35 fighter jets.

items.h: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority warns of legal action against Sinokor's entire fleet starting November 1
items.t: Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority said on X on October 27 that vessels of South Korea's Sinokor Merchant Marine had committed the most transit violations in the Strait of Hormuz over the past three months, that it had already acted against seven of them, and that it would take legal action against all of the company's ships starting November 1. The Korea Shipowners' Association said on October 28 that the vessels in question are not owned by Sinokor but sub-chartered to an overseas oil company and carry no South Korean crew, Reuters reported.

items.h: Likud leads partial count in Israel's election as neither bloc secures a majority
items.t: With about 40 percent of ballots counted in Israel's October 27 election, the Central Elections Committee's partial results gave Likud 21.70 percent and Yashar, led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot, 15.72 percent, the AP reported. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu claimed early on October 28 that the right-wing bloc had won a decisive majority among the Zionist and Jewish public. The final tally is due by October 30, and official results will be published November 4.

items.h: Finnish and Norwegian leaders relay negotiation messages to Putin ahead of Abu Dhabi talks
items.t: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre said they spoke with Russian President Vladimir Putin on October 27, in consultation with Ukraine, to convey messages on future negotiations, and that the call was linked to an upcoming meeting in Abu Dhabi. The Kyiv Independent reported that trilateral U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks are expected in Abu Dhabi sometime in November.

items.h: IAEA's Grossi tells Security Council Iran is not providing access to verify its highly enriched uranium
items.t: IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi told a UN Security Council meeting on October 27 that Iran has not provided the information and access needed to verify its declared nuclear material, singling out about 440 kilograms of highly enriched uranium as a particular concern. He said the agency had not detected any repair or reconstruction work at the struck facilities since June 2025.

items.h: Pezeshkian meets Putin in Moscow as Qatar urges Iran to reopen the strait
items.t: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met Russian President Vladimir Putin on October 27 on the sidelines of the Gas Exporting Countries Forum summit in Moscow and said the region can resolve its problems without relying on the United States, AFP reported. Qatar's emir, Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani, also met him in Moscow that day, and Qatari foreign ministry official Ibrahim Al-Hashmi said Iran must demonstrate good faith and reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

items.h: Russia and Ukraine begin local ceasefire around Oleshky, brokered by Melania Trump
items.t: Ukraine's parliamentary human rights commissioner, Dmytro Lubinets, said a ceasefire to allow aid deliveries and civilian evacuations took effect around Oleshky in Kherson Oblast at 3 a.m. Kyiv time on October 27, and Russia's Defense Ministry said its forces stopped firing in the Kherson direction at 4 a.m. Moscow time. The AP reported that the pause is due to last at least through Saturday and that a new round of U.S.-brokered Russia-Ukraine talks is expected next month.

items.h: Russian ballistic missile strike on Kyiv kills one, injures 10 including university dorm students
items.t: A Russian ballistic missile attack on Kyiv late on October 26 killed one person and injured 10, including students in a university dormitory, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. Ukraine's Air Force had warned that several ballistic missiles launched from the direction of Bryansk were heading for the capital; schools and medical facilities were among the sites damaged.

items.h: Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani security chiefs meet Iran's leaders in Tehran, agree to keep talking
items.t: Saudi Defense Minister Khalid bin Salman, Pakistani army chief Asim Munir and Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met President Masoud Pezeshkian and other Iranian leaders in Tehran on October 26. Iranian state media said the four countries agreed to continue talks on strengthening cooperation; no concrete agreement was announced.

items.h: Egypt's parliament authorizes Sisi to help defend Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks
items.t: Egypt's House of Representatives on October 26 authorized President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi to take the measures needed to support Saudi Arabia, Al-Ahram reported. The authorization is conditional on a request from Riyadh, and Sisi had said earlier that any support would be limited to defending Saudi territory and borders and would not include attacks on Yemen.

items.h: Iran's military chief warns ships that stray from designated routes in southern waters will face damage
items.t: Maj. Gen. Ali Abdollahi, chief of the general staff of Iran's armed forces, said on October 26 during a visit to the Gulf of Oman coast that any vessel that, for any reason, strays from designated routes or ignores Iranian procedures is putting itself at risk and will suffer serious damage, Press TV reported.

items.h: Romanian intelligence blames September fire near Brasov arms plant on Russian-run sabotage network
items.t: The Romanian Intelligence Service (SRI) and anti-organized crime and terrorism prosecutors (DIICOT) said on October 26 that a fire on September 14 near Carfil, a subsidiary of state arms maker Romarm in Brasov, was the work of a Russian-directed sabotage network. Two of the three suspects (two Belarusians and a Ukrainian) were arrested in Germany; no casualties were reported.

items.h: Jordan strikes southern Syria after church shooting; Damascus denies prior coordination
items.t: Jordan's armed forces said they struck hideouts of armed groups in southeastern Syria on October 26 in coordination with the Syrian government, but Damascus disputed that, saying there had been no prior coordination or notice. Syria's Civil Defense said at least seven people, including three children, were killed in Daraa and Sweida provinces.

items.h: Kim Jong Un makes day trip to China's Dandong, greeted by Wang Huning
items.t: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un crossed the New Yalu River Bridge on October 24 for a one-day visit to Dandong in China's Liaoning province, laying a wreath at the memorial to China's Korean War intervention and touring a car factory, according to Xinhua (October 24) and KCNA (October 25). Wang Huning, chairman of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, received him and saw him off; no meeting with Xi Jinping was reported.

items.h: Kremlin aide Ushakov says U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks can resume after November 4
items.t: Yuri Ushakov, the Kremlin's foreign policy aide, told Russian TV channel Vesti on October 25 that the next deadline is November 4, a Russian national holiday, and that Moscow is ready to resume talks after that. He said the first meeting would be preliminary, RBC reported.

items.h: Trump on new Iran strikes: "maybe tomorrow" — then "There will not be a strike today"
items.t: Asked on October 24 (local time) whether the U.S. would strike Iran again, President Trump told reporters, "We're thinking about doing it, and maybe tomorrow." On October 25, at the White House before leaving for a rally in Michigan, he said, "There will not be a strike today." He did not say whether he had made a decision.

items.h: Houthis claim strikes on Aramco site in Yanbu; Saudi Arabia says it intercepted missiles
items.t: Yemen's Houthis claimed on October 24 that they struck an Aramco facility in Yanbu, the Rabigh refinery and other targets in Saudi Arabia; no damage has been confirmed. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed at Yanbu and Taif on October 24 and 10 aimed at southern Saudi Arabia on October 25, among others.

items.h: Iran says it is trading messages with the U.S. through intermediaries
items.t: Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei told a German broadcaster that Iran remains open to diplomacy and is passing messages to the U.S. through intermediaries, but that Iran cannot accept demands for "complete surrender," Iranian state media reported. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on October 25 that Iran's policies stay the same whether or not there is war.

items.h: North Korea claims to UN Security Council that South staged DMZ mine blast
items.t: North Korea sent a letter on October 25 to the president of the UN Security Council calling the September 21 mine explosion in the DMZ a South Korean fabrication and warning that it would exercise its right of self-defense if its territory or personnel were violated, KCNA reported on October 26. North Korean media have not reported the South Korean Defense Ministry's October 23 proposal for military talks.

items.h: Student movement wins Serbia's election as Vučić concedes defeat
items.t: Former President Aleksandar Vučić conceded defeat in Serbia's October 25 parliamentary election, citing a sample count. He said the Student List would win 135 to 140 of the 250 seats and his own camp about 105.

items.h: Lula wins a fourth term in Brazil's presidential runoff
items.t: Brazil's Superior Electoral Court declared President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva the winner of the October 25 runoff with 51.76 percent of the vote against 48.24 percent for Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, a margin of more than 4 million votes.

items.h: Machado returns to Venezuela after more than 10 months in exile
items.t: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned home on October 25 after more than 10 months in exile and greeted supporters at a church in Lara state. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said her return was the result of U.S.-backed reconciliation talks.

items.h: Cargo ship sinks after drone strike just outside Romanian waters; Romania's president blames Russia
items.t: The Comoros-flagged cargo ship Khoryv sank on October 23 after a drone strike about 13 nautical miles off the Romanian port of Constanta, just beyond Romania's territorial waters. One Ukrainian sailor was killed and three crew members are missing. Romanian President Nicusor Dan called the attack part of Russia's escalation of its war in Ukraine; Russia had not publicly responded.

items.h: Trump on Iran: "We may do another little Epic Fury"
items.t: At a rally in Fort Myers, Florida, on October 23, President Trump said of the Iran war, "We may do another little Epic Fury, or they'll agree." Operation Epic Fury is the U.S. military's name for its campaign against Iran.

items.h: Asked about a weekend strike on Iran, U.S. ambassador Barrack says "absolutely"; Trump says he knows nothing about it
items.t: Asked in an interview released October 23 whether a strike could come this weekend, Tom Barrack, the U.S. ambassador to Turkey, answered, "Absolutely." Trump said the same day that he didn't know anything about it. He had said earlier that a strike would not come before the November 3 midterm elections.

items.h: Zelensky says technical-level U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks are planned in Abu Dhabi for the first half of November
items.t: In a video address to the Hudson Institute on October 23, President Zelensky said negotiating teams from the U.S., Russia and Ukraine plan to meet in Abu Dhabi in the first half of November. If the technical-level talks are productive, he said, they should move to a meeting of leaders; an October meeting fell through because Russia cited other reasons.

items.h: Ukraine and Russia agree to a local ceasefire around Oleshky, mediated by Melania Trump
items.t: The White House and Ukraine's human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, said on October 23 that first lady Melania Trump had mediated a local ceasefire around Russian-occupied Oleshky in Kherson Oblast. The truce is meant to allow civilian evacuations and aid deliveries. Russia's General Staff said it would begin at 4 a.m. local time on October 27; the White House gave the start date as October 29.

items.h: State Department cuts embassy staff in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the UAE over Houthi threat
items.t: The State Department said on October 23 that it is reducing staff at its embassies in Jordan, Lebanon, Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, which will remain open, citing concerns about Houthi rocket, missile and drone attacks, CBS reported. Nonessential staff at the U.S. Embassy in Saudi Arabia were ordered to leave earlier in the week.

items.h: Brent settles at $116.72, its highest close since April 29
items.t: Brent crude futures settled at $116.72 a barrel on October 23, up 3.14 percent, and U.S. West Texas Intermediate closed at $103.27, up 3.8 percent, according to Reuters. Reuters said Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia stoked fears of supply disruptions.

items.h: Waltz on the prospect of another year of war in Iran: "One would hope" Tehran comes to the table first
items.t: Asked by the Financial Times whether the Iran war could last another year, Mike Waltz, the U.S. ambassador to the United Nations, declined to speculate but said, "One would hope that they'll come to the table in a meaningful way before that." He added that the U.S. Navy can maintain the naval blockade of Iran for the foreseeable future.

items.h: Ukraine and Russia swap 270 prisoners each, the first exchange in two months
items.t: President Zelensky said on October 23 that 270 Ukrainian prisoners of war had come home and 270 Russian POWs had been returned to Russia. It was the first swap since August; most of the returning Ukrainians were captured during the 2022 siege of Mariupol.

items.h: Seoul proposes military talks with North Korea to verify the MDL and restore hotlines
items.t: In a statement on the afternoon of October 23, Kim Hong-cheol, South Korea's deputy minister for national defense policy, formally proposed military talks with the North to jointly verify where the land Military Demarcation Line lies, restore military communication lines and discuss ways to prevent accidental clashes along the border. He said three-way talks including the UN Command were also possible.

items.h: Trump on Iran: "We may do it a little bit further"
items.t: Speaking to reporters at the White House on October 22 before leaving for a rally in Iowa, President Trump said, "We've knocked the hell out of them, and we may do it a little bit further." He added, "We can't let Iran have a nuclear weapon."

items.h: Trump claims Iran is "making up fake hits, mines" to push up oil prices
items.t: In a Truth Social post on October 22, Trump claimed Iran "is doing everything they can to drive up the price of Oil prior to the U.S. Midterm Election" and is "making up fake hits, mines, and everything else." Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed the same day that four tankers had been hit and three had struck mines; the claims could not be independently verified.

items.h: IRGC threatens U.S. bases over Hormuz tanker transits
items.t: The IRGC warned on October 22, in a statement on its Sepah News site, that U.S. help for tankers transiting the strait could widen the war: "If this trend continues, the conflict will extend to its bases in the region." A U.S. Central Command spokesperson, speaking to Al Jazeera on condition of anonymity, called the mine claims incorrect and said 95 percent of vessels are getting through.

items.h: Brent settles at $113, its highest close since early May
items.t: Brent crude rose 4.0 percent on October 22 to settle at $113.17 a barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate crude gained 2.4 percent to $99.47. It was Brent's highest settlement since May 4.

items.h: Saudi airport attack death toll rises to two; coalition intercepts missile aimed at Najran
items.t: Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said on October 22 that the death toll from the attack on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam had risen to two. The Saudi-led coalition said the same day it had intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Najran, and AFP, citing sources, reported that Aramco told essential staff at its Dhahran headquarters to evacuate.

items.h: Reuters: U.S. and South Korean officials see little chance of a Trump-Kim meeting this year
items.t: Citing five people familiar with the matter, Reuters reported that U.S. and South Korean officials see little chance of a meeting this year between Trump and North Korean leader Kim Jong Un. The sources said Washington has received no response from Pyongyang on holding one.

items.h: Zelensky: Kyiv strike right after talks shows "no real change" in Russia's attitude
items.t: Zelensky said on social media on October 22 that Russia fired 21 ballistic missiles at Kyiv in three waves from the evening of October 21 into the early hours of October 22 (local time), and also used three ballistic missiles fitted with cluster warheads. He said 12 regions came under attack and 34 people were wounded, five of them children.

items.h: Kremlin says Abu Dhabi is the venue under discussion for three-way talks
items.t: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said on October 22 that "at this point, we are talking about Abu Dhabi" as the venue for talks among Russia, the U.S. and Ukraine. Asked whether Russia's negotiators were preparing documents or proposals, he declined to say, telling reporters not to get ahead of themselves.

items.h: Kremlin says it is ready to resume three-way talks around November 10 after Witkoff meeting
items.t: After Putin met U.S. envoy Steve Witkoff in St. Petersburg on October 21, presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said Russia is ready in principle to resume three-way talks with the U.S. and Ukraine around November 10. Russia freed jailed American Stephen Hubbard, 74, as the meeting began.

items.h: Zelensky hopes for U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks by early November
items.t: On his way back to Kyiv from Norway, Zelensky told reporters he believes the three-way talks should take place no later than early November (Al Jazeera, October 21). Ushakov told Russian state TV channel Vesti the talks could be held in Abu Dhabi.

items.h: Netanyahu says toppling Iran's regime is the only way to end its threat
items.t: Speaking at an Israeli military officers' graduation ceremony on October 21, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said the only way to remove Iran's threat for good is to overthrow the regime. He said he had issued directives to the military, the Mossad and other security services but did not say what they were.

items.h: State Department orders non-emergency staff and families out of Saudi Arabia over Houthi attacks
items.t: State Department spokesperson Tommy Pigott said on X on October 21 that the department had ordered non-emergency employees and their families to leave Saudi Arabia, citing attacks by the Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi airports and infrastructure. Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority said an attack late on October 21 on King Fahd International Airport in Dammam killed one person and injured eight.

items.h: IRGC spokesman warns Iran will respond and go on the offensive if attacked
items.t: In an October 21 interview with the Student News Network, IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said the Guards' doctrine, which had been largely defensive, now includes offensive action, and that any country that attacks Iran will face both a response and an offensive, IranWire reported.

items.h: Kim Yo Jong says loudspeakers aimed at South Korea will be on standby within days
items.t: In an October 22 statement carried by KCNA, Kim Yo Jong, director of the Workers' Party's General Affairs Department, said North Korea's new means of response will go on mission standby along the entire border and its loudspeakers aimed at South Korea will be on standby within days. In an October 21 statement, she said the loudspeakers would be operating along the entire border sometime in October.

items.h: Russian ballistic missiles and drones hit Kyiv overnight October 21–22, injuring 15
items.t: Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko said Russian ballistic missile and drone attacks overnight on October 21–22 (local time) injured 15 people, including two 15-year-olds. Metro infrastructure on the Pivdennyi Bridge and an ambulance station in the Pecherskyi district were damaged.

items.h: Moscow mayor reports downing drones overnight October 21–22; TASS tallies 630
items.t: Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported downing wave after wave of Ukrainian drones headed for Moscow between 8:30 p.m. on October 21 and 4 a.m. on October 22 (Moscow time); TASS, tallying his announcements, put the total at 630. He said 163 were downed as they approached the city, and two people were injured near Voronovo.

items.h: U.S. Embassy in Canada accuses Canadian politicians of trying to sway the midterms
items.t: In a fact sheet released October 21, the U.S. Embassy in Canada claimed that Industry Minister Mélanie Joly, Ontario Premier Doug Ford and others are trying to influence the November 3 U.S. midterm elections through their responses to President Donald Trump's tariffs. Joly had denied any interference on October 14, saying her work in the U.S. was aimed at attracting investment.

digest.t: North Korea answers talks offer with missiles as allied security meeting slips to 2027
digest.d: North Korea fired around 10 short-range ballistic missiles into the East Sea from the Wonsan area at about 12:30 p.m. on October 29, according to South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff. The launch came six days after South Korea's Defense Ministry proposed military talks on October 23 to confirm the Military Demarcation Line and restore military communication lines; North Korea has not responded to the offer. The Korean Central News Agency reported on November 1 that North Korea had tested a cluster-bomb warhead for tactical ballistic missiles. North Korea fired several more missiles into the East Sea from the Sondok area of South Hamgyong province on the morning of November 4, and the Korean Central News Agency reported that it had tested a new anti-aircraft missile and a long-range strategic cruise missile aimed at a mock airfield target that day. In a statement the same day, Kim Yo Jong, a vice department director of the Workers' Party, said dialogue is among the options for safeguarding peace but is not necessarily the same as the national interest. The South Korean and U.S. defense chiefs met in Cebu, the Philippines, on October 28 and agreed to push the 58th Security Consultative Meeting, which had been expected this fall, to early 2027; the Pentagon cited scheduling conflicts among senior officials.

digest.t: Blockade on Iran extends overland as bridge proposals leave a deal distant
digest.d: U.S. Central Command launched Task Force Iron Gate on November 7 to block the movement of goods across Iran's land borders and the Caspian Sea, and the same day it struck and stopped the cargo ship Huda in the Gulf of Oman. President Trump said on the 6th that U.S. forces had hit air-defense equipment on Qeshm Island, calling it a "minor" strike. Middle Eastern officials told the AP that Qatar had put forward a two-day bridge proposal: on the first day the United States would lift its blockade and release part of Iran's frozen funds while Iran allowed inspections of its bombed nuclear sites, and on the second day the strait would reopen. But Secretary of State Rubio said on the 8th that some of Iran's demands were outrageous and unrealistic, adding that he would not say the two sides were on the verge of a breakthrough. Ships keep getting hit in the strait, and the International Maritime Organization says at least 25 seafarers have been killed since late February. Brent crude fell to the $94 range on the 4th on hopes of a ceasefire after the midterm elections, then settled in the $98 range on the 6th.

digest.t: Houthis target an Aramco building in Riyadh as civilian deaths mount in Yemen
digest.d: The Houthis fired missiles at the Saudi capital, Riyadh, on the morning of November 8. Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said the attack targeted an Aramco building and that falling debris caused limited damage, with no casualties. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted missiles headed for Riyadh; the Houthis claimed to have struck Aramco facilities including Abqaiq, but the claim has not been confirmed. On the 6th, an attack on a market in Yemen's Taiz province killed at least 30 people; the Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia, while the Saudi-backed government side blamed the Houthis.

digest.t: Eisenkot gets the mandate to form Israel's government after a 67-46 split in nominations
digest.d: President Herzog formally tasked Gadi Eisenkot with forming a government at the President's Residence in Jerusalem on November 8. After finishing consultations with the parties on the 5th, Herzog said 67 Knesset members had recommended Eisenkot and 46 had recommended Prime Minister Netanyahu; United Torah Judaism, with seven seats, did not recommend Netanyahu. The lawmakers backing Eisenkot include the 19 members of the two Arab parties. Eisenkot has 28 days to form a government, which can be extended by up to 14 days. Netanyahu denounced it as a government relying on Islamists and called for a national unity government. The new Knesset opens on the 10th.

digest.t: Democrats take both chambers of Congress as Republicans split over the cost of the Iran war
digest.d: Democrats won majorities in both the Senate and the House in the November 3 midterm elections. According to the AP count as of the 7th, Democrats hold 54 Senate seats to the Republicans' 44, with Mississippi and Alaska still undecided, and 254 House seats to 162. Vice President Vance on the 4th pointed to the Iran war as the reason for the defeat, while President Trump cited gasoline prices and poor messaging. The new Congress, which convenes in January 2027, can pass a war powers resolution by a simple majority, but overriding a presidential veto requires two-thirds of both chambers. On the 5th, the Nasdaq fell 5.52 percent on concerns that a Democratic Congress would move to regulate artificial intelligence.

digest.t: U.S.-China summitry projects calm, but allies pay the price
digest.d: With Trump's visit to China in May and Xi Jinping's visit to the United States in September, the U.S.-China tariff truce was extended to January 2027. Over the same period, Washington floated arms sales to Taiwan as a bargaining chip, unilaterally scaled back joint South Korea-U.S. exercises, and slapped Section 301 tariffs on allies as well.

digest.t: U.S.-China AI chip race rolls on despite the truce
digest.d: The U.S.-China summit in September extended the tariff truce to January 10, 2027, but kept chip export controls off the agenda. Samsung Electronics and SK hynix are running their plants in China on one-year U.S. licenses that expire at the end of the year, and China has put in place a legal basis for sanctioning companies that comply with U.S. controls. Meanwhile, China's CXMT has lifted its share of the DRAM market from 4 percent to 10 percent in a single year.

digest.t: U.S., Russian and Ukrainian delegations head to Abu Dhabi amid heavy strikes on energy
digest.d: Kremlin spokesman Peskov confirmed on November 3 that a Russian delegation would attend the U.S.-Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi on the 10th and 11th. Presidential aide Medinsky leads the Russian delegation and Umerov the Ukrainian one. In an interview with CBS's 60 Minutes, President Trump said Ukraine would end up with a little bit different shape after the war and that a deal was very close. Meanwhile, on the 3rd Russia attacked Ukraine's energy facilities with 289 drones and 76 missiles, targeting even a substation that supplies the Khmelnytskyi nuclear plant, and Kyiv suffered its worst water outage since the full-scale war began. The death toll from the November 2 bombing of an aid distribution point in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, has risen to 53.

digest.t: Russia targets Black Sea cargo ships as Poland reinforces the Kaliningrad border
digest.d: Russia's Defense Ministry claimed on November 8 that it had struck three cargo ships and two substations near the ports of Odesa and Chornomorsk in Ukraine's Odesa region; Reuters could not independently verify the claim. Polish Prime Minister Tusk said on the 3rd that the Border Guard had reported worrying movements along the Kaliningrad border and that police and troops, including counterterrorism units, had been reinforced in the Warmian-Masurian and Podlaskie provinces for a special operation. In early November, Latvia's army warned of a threat in the airspace over its eastern regions and told residents to stay indoors. Earlier, on October 26, Romania's Intelligence Service announced that a September fire near an arms company in Brașov was sabotage coordinated by Russia.

In August, Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan signed the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement, and on October 5 the three countries invoked "collective deterrence measures" against Houthi attacks and decided to deploy forces rapidly to Saudi Arabia. The Turkish Grand National Assembly ratified the pact on November 5 by 279 votes to 119. North Korea, already bound to Russia by the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership Treaty it signed in 2024, has also restored relations with China following Xi Jinping's visit to Pyongyang in June. On October 30, Canada and the EU launched an "Alliance for the Future," agreeing to work toward making Canada the EU's first associate member and to expand cooperation on defense procurement, space and critical minerals. Armenian Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said on November 6 that Armenia's interest in the Russia-led Collective Security Treaty Organization was over.

digest.t: Pakistan faces two fronts, east and west, and an emergency in its northwest
digest.d: Pakistan has been fighting the Taliban government in Afghanistan since February, and after strikes on Kandahar in late September it bombed Kunar and Helmand provinces on the night of September 30. The UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan said the strikes killed at least 10 civilians, most of them children. On the Indian front, Pakistani and Indian warships collided in the Arabian Sea on September 15. A court of arbitration has ruled on the Indus Waters Treaty, but India does not recognize the court's jurisdiction. President Zardari declared a state of emergency in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa on October 11, citing a surge in militant activity in the northwest. On October 17, Pakistani forces and the Afghan Taliban clashed at several points along the border around Kurram.

digest.t: Washington puts the Monroe Doctrine into practice
digest.d: In January the U.S. military captured President Maduro, and the United States then signed an oil agreement with Venezuela's transitional government. Washington has imposed an energy blockade on Cuba since January and is waging tariff wars with Canada and Brazil. In September it signed a security agreement on Greenland with Denmark. On October 14, a report said a U.S. Army battalion had begun deploying to Panama for counter-cartel training; Southern Command did not comment on the deployment. On October 21, the U.S. Embassy in Canada alleged that Canadian politicians were trying to interfere in the U.S. midterm elections. Venezuelan opposition leader Machado returned home on October 25 after more than 10 months in exile, and acting President Rodríguez said on the 29th that elections would be held but gave no date. In Brazil, President Lula won a fourth term with 51.79 percent in the October 25 runoff. On November 5 the U.S. State Department sanctioned two individuals, eight entities including two Chinese companies, and five tankers over the Cuban regime's foreign military support and illicit revenue networks; China's Commerce Ministry objected on the 7th. There were also reports that Washington is negotiating a status-of-forces agreement with Venezuela's interim government that could open the way to a long-term U.S. military presence.

digest.t: Wars flare at once across the Horn of Africa and the Sahel
digest.d: The Tigray war resumed on September 22, and on October 6 and 7 a string of witness accounts said Eritrean troops had crossed the border and entered towns in northern Tigray. In a letter dated October 8, Ethiopian Foreign Minister Gedion Timothewos called this an "all-out invasion" and cited the right of self-defense; the Eritrean government denied it and countered that Ethiopia has designs on the port of Assab. Sudan's civil war and the offensives of jihadist insurgents in the Sahel continue. On October 19, a drone attack on a market and a fuel depot in Abyei, an area contested by Sudan and South Sudan, killed at least 153 people. In September, Yemen's Houthi rebels seized the port of Mocha and Perim Island, tightening their grip on the Bab el-Mandeb Strait at the mouth of the Red Sea. Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy said on October 28 that the country had received 12 Russian-made Su-35 fighter jets and planned to acquire the S-400 air defense system. In Sudan, an October 26 airstrike on a market in Nyala, Darfur, killed many civilians, with death tolls ranging from 21 to more than 100 depending on the group counting. In Somalia, President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud dismissed the chief justice and named a successor on the 4th, and on the 5th the Supreme Court ruled that the extension of his term was unlawful and that the dismissal was beyond his authority. Ethiopia and Sudan closed each other's consulates and expelled diplomats in early November.

learn.t: Why has the armed stalemate on the Korean Peninsula lasted so long?
learn.d: In On War, Book 3, Chapter 16, Clausewitz wrote that military action can stand still for a long time when both sides think waiting works in their favor, or when defense is stronger than attack. On the Korean Peninsula, for South Korea, the United States and North Korea alike, the cost of changing the status quo outweighs the cost of waiting. But as Glenn Snyder's stability-instability paradox of 1965 points out, a stalemate under nuclear deterrence is not calm: local clashes like the Cheonan sinking and the Yeonpyeong shelling of 2010 can still break out. Clisa Geopolitics believes agreements here have only bought time within the stalemate rather than ending it, as with the 1994 Agreed Framework, which froze Yongbyon for eight years and then collapsed once North Korea got around it through uranium enrichment.

cur.why: There is no room for a deal on sovereignty. forces: China's pressure below the threshold of war

Below the threshold of war, China is widening its de facto control through exercises, the coast guard and maritime jurisdiction. In 2026 coast guard patrols, rather than large named exercises, have carried the pressure, and on November 10 Taiwan's defense minister confirmed that China had held unannounced "area denial" drills in the western Pacific with the Liaoning carrier group.

In 2026 there has not been a single large named exercise, and two days after KMT chair Cheng Li-wun met Xi Jinping in April, China announced 10 measures including normalizing direct flights.
Taiwanese voters answered coercion before the 1996 and 2000 elections with backlash votes, and unification talks made no progress even under KMT rule (2008–2016).
Coast guard pressure and inducements to Taiwan's opposition would both continue, without a blockade or fighting, until the January 2028 election.

allison
The structural pressure created by the shift in power between the United States and China makes it easy for routine crises in the strait to escalate into war, even if neither side wants it.

Each crisis has raised the level of pressure: China's effective erasure of the median line in 2022, its regular coast guard patrols in Kinmen waters since 2024, and the Guangdong Maritime Safety Administration's demand in August 2026 to control passage.
No strait crisis since 1954 has escalated into war, and the U.S. and Chinese leaders visited each other in May and September and extended their tariff truce until January 10, 2027.
Crises in the strait would merge with China's disputes with Japan and the Philippines and spread along alliance lines.

That is why Clisa Geopolitics divides a ceasefire on the current front into a Korean model, with guarantees, and a Minsk model, without them.
